Architecture

How the pieces fit: from the files to the GPU cube, the series and Zeit's methods, and what each crate and module of the program does.

On this page

  1. Crates
  2. The program (crates/janus-app/src)
  3. Elsewhere
Install Usage Architecture Building README
 files (GDAL) ──► Overview (CPU, [t][y][x] float32) ──► GPU cube (wgpu: R32F texture array)
       │               │ disk cache (.januscube)                       │
       │               └─ instant approximate series                   ├─► statistics (compute shader, 1 pass)
       │                                                               └─► display shader (stretch, colormap, modes)
       ├──► FullResCache: every date at full resolution on the local disk (built with the overview on an HDD)
       │         └─ read first by the two below for the dates it has
       ├──► detail tiles of the visible area at full resolution ──► LRU on the GPU
       └──► exact pixel series / ROI (interactive pool, cancellable)

 XYZ tiles (GDAL WMS/TMS, curl) ──► Basemap: tiles of the view at the screen's zoom ──► LRU on the GPU,
                                    drawn first, through a warp grid (active layer's grid -> EPSG:3857)

 vector files (OGR) ──► VectorData (file coordinates) ──► placed on the active layer's grid (PROJ)
                                                          ├─► drawn over every map panel
                                                          ├─► a polygon as the ROI (pixel-centre mask)
                                                          └─► series extracted / interpretation labels

 a series or a window of it ──► Zeit's methods (zeit-core and janus-zeit, in the process, on every core)
                                ├─► a pixel: the model on the chart, its numbers in Statistics (< 1 ms)
                                └─► a raster run: result maps as layers, series as new layers

The interface is egui (with egui_dock for the panels and egui_plot for the charts) on wgpu: Direct3D 12, Vulkan or Metal. Long work runs on thread pools; a GDAL dataset is never shared between threads (each thread has its readers).

Crates

CrateRole
janus-cubeA series as a cube: layer, date and band discovery (folders, wildcards, multiband files, NetCDF/Zarr/HDF variables and levels, URLs and cloud buckets through GDAL's network file systems), spectra (wavelengths from the band metadata or EnMAP's METADATA.XML), band roles, per-thread readers (nodata → NaN, scale/offset, normalized difference, quality masks), the statistics of a pixel's series and an ROI's values, the series as a VRT
janus-gdalThe few GDAL C functions the gdal crate does not cover
janus-cacheThe overview (built in parallel, following the focused date) and its disk cache; the full-resolution cache (lossless 64 × 64 blocks per date); the disk budget they share; the thread pool with priorities. The files are the same as the C++ versions'
janus-sessionOne open series: the pools (background and interactive), exact series, ROI, detail tiles, spinning-disk detection
janus-gpuThe map on the GPU: the cube, the per-pixel statistics (stats.wgsl), the display modes (display.wgsl), class tables, warp grids, render targets per map panel and their readback; the colormaps
janus-geoLayers in another CRS or on a rotated grid (exact PROJ transformation and the warp grid the shader samples through), the web basemap (XYZ tiles through GDAL, an LRU of textures), plane geometry (polygons as even-odd rings, masks of pixel centres), vector files through OGR
janus-mlDeep learning on Burn (the GPU through the same wgpu as the map, or the CPU): samples read from the cube at full resolution, gaps filled and scaled the way sits does it, TempCNN and L-TAE as their authors built them (Pelletier et al. 2019; Garnot & Landrieu 2020), Presto and U-TAE with their authors' weights (read from their PyTorch files), their training (stratified split, AdamW, early stopping), the .janusmodel file, and a model applied to a window in row bands or, for U-TAE, overlapping windows (class map, probability, entropy)
janus-zeitZeit's tools in the process: their descriptors (tools.json), a pixel fit, a raster run over a window in row bands (outputs as GeoTIFFs, series outputs, the run's log), the run's time estimated on a sample, Copy Python (the Zeit calls a fit makes, as code); the methods are zeit-core's, with the glue the Python bridge had (bands by role, NDFI, CODED, Tmask, the BFAST family's refits, SOM, TWDTW, the agreement of change maps, SNIC's segmentation by rows of tiles and its polygons)
janus-embedFoundation-model embeddings (AlphaEarth, TESSERA): the store (every year at reduced resolution, Int8), SIMD kernels chosen at run time (AVX2 + FMA, SSE2, NEON), PCA by subspace iteration, similarity and change, exports at full resolution, the download of an area
janus-validationValidation after Olofsson et al. (2014) and Stehman (2014), without an interface: maps read by a rule (classes, intervals, events), strata in one parallel pass at full resolution (other maps warped onto the first's grid, a buffer, a polygon limit, areas on the sphere in a geographic CRS), the design (eq. 13, allocations), the seeded draw, the estimators, dates, kappa, the project in a GeoPackage, the reference of a point from several interpreters, the Python that reproduces the estimates
janus-appThe program (janus, and jn, the command line)

The program (crates/janus-app/src)

ModuleRole
main.rsOptions, the bundled data (PROJ, GDAL, plugins, CA certificates), the window
app.rsThe state, the dock of panels (default layout, kept between sessions), panels in windows of their own, menus, shortcuts
map.rs, views.rsThe map (every layer drawn by the GPU into a target, marks, input), map panels and the swipe
panels.rs, display.rs, layers.rs, files.rs, settings.rs, theme.rsDisplay, Layers, Files, Statistics, Performance and Settings; the seven themes and the fonts (ProggyClean at 13 px, ProggyForever at other sizes)
series.rs, chart.rs, roi.rs, season.rsThe series on the chart (cursor, pins, ROI, other layers'), the chart, the ROI's shape, the season and temporal composites
classes.rs, composite.rs, analysis.rs, transect.rsCategorical series, RGB composites of three bands, the Analysis panel, the space-time transect
vectors.rs, vector_gpu.rs, vector_pick.rs, vector_labels.rs, labels.rsVector layers (placing, drawing, picking, extracting series), their levels of detail on the GPU, the grid of their boxes for picking, their labels; interpretation (TimeSync style)
zeit.rs, python.rsThe Tools menu, a panel per tool made from its descriptor, fits on the chart, Tasks, Log, result layers; Copy Python
embeddings.rs, emb_download.rsEmbeddings in the interface and their download for the visible area
validation.rs, validation_tabs.rs, chips.rsThe Validation menu and panel, the project's sample as a vector layer, blind interpretation, Chips
export_map.rs, canvas.rs, exports.rs, animation.rs, gif.rsExports (PNG figures drawn on a CPU canvas, GeoTIFFs, results), the Exports window, animations (GIF without a library, MP4/WebM through ffmpeg)
basemap.rs, open.rs, platform.rsThe basemap in the interface, Open URL and multidimensional files, what depends on the system
ui_test*.rs, selftest_zeit.rs, embeddings_test.rs, measure*.rs, tour.rs, golden.rs--selftest-ui, --selftest-zeit, --selftest-embeddings-ui, --measure-cache, --measure-vectors, --profile-tour, --dump-golden
shots.rs, shots_validation.rs--shots: the website guides' screenshots
bin/jn.rsjn: prints --help and --version to the terminal, else opens the interface and returns

Elsewhere

PathRole
tools/package.pyThe packages: Windows installer (installer/janus.iss, Inno Setup), Linux .tar.xz, macOS .dmg; each with LICENSE and THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.txt
tools/notices.pyTHIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.txt: the crates in the program, the conda-forge libraries and data a package carries, the fonts, with their license texts
tools/make_selftest_data.pySynthetic inputs for the self-tests
tools/make_tutorial_data.py, tools/make_guide_data.pyReal data for the website's guides and their screenshots
tools/zeit_fixtures.py, tools/zeit_raster_fixtures.pyThe expected results of Zeit's Python, against which janus-zeit's tests check the tools
.github/workflows/build.ymlCI: Windows, Linux and macOS builds, tests, self-tests, packages; releases on v* tags
site/The website (GitHub Pages)
RUST_MIGRATION.mdHow Janus moved from C++ to Rust (0.39 → 1.0), with the measures
